description: Machine-readable samples for the five-part bullet parser prompt (parser-prompt.md next to this file). Use with any model: send the rules plus the acceptance examples, then one entry's 'original' at a time, and compare the model's brackets with 'expected'. 'status': ok = filled with exact words, vague = filled with the words but marked vague, missing = empty brackets. v1.1.0: rules updated 2026-11-03 with research-verb classification (Problem 2), third-party features and intention-clause phrases (Problem 1), and display/score consistency (Problem 6); no sample outputs changed. v1.2.0: display format is now ONE continuous sentence with in-sentence brackets (see display_frame); section data and statuses unchanged. v1.3.0: moved with the prompt to specs/001-experience-improvement-flow/few-shot/ (single source of truth beside the spec); no sample changes.

acceptance_examples.original: Analyzed job seekers’ needs and the absence of a talent pool and job postings, and collaborated with the product team to define the MVP scope (resume analysis and resume-to-job matching) through 6 job-seeker interviews and a 30-respondent questionnaire, aiming to deliver value without depending on employers

user_need.text: Analyzed job seekers’ needs and the absence of a talent pool and job postings

product_feature.text: the MVP scope (resume analysis and resume-to-job matching)

action.text: collaborated with the product team to define the MVP scope (resume analysis and resume-to-job matching) through 6 job-seeker interviews and a 30-respondent questionnaire

result.text: aiming to deliver value without depending on employers

needs_to_be_filled: User need or problem (vague): “Analyzed job seekers’ needs” says what you studied, but not who had which problem. “The absence of a talent pool and job postings” describes a limit of the product, not a problem of the job seeker.
Result (vague): “aiming to deliver value” is a goal. It does not say what changed after your work or who it helped.
Metric (missing, optional): “6 job-seeker interviews” and “a 30-respondent questionnaire” describe your research, so they stay in Action.
acceptance_examples.first_question_after_yes: Achievement 1 of 1 – User need or problem: Who had a problem? What was the problem?

acceptance_examples.original: Worked on the onboarding flow and made it better, which reduced drop-off by 18% in the first week

action.text: Worked on the onboarding flow and made it better

needs_to_be_filled: User need or problem (missing): The bullet does not say who struggled or what went wrong.
Action (vague): “Worked on” and “made it better” do not say what you did or what your role was.
acceptance_examples.first_question_after_yes: Achievement 2 of 3 – User need or problem: Who had a problem? What was the problem?

acceptance_examples.original: New users could not find the items they saved, so I wrote the requirements and worked with the design team to rebuild the saved items page, and return visits grew by 15%

user_need.text: New users could not find the items they saved

action.text: I wrote the requirements and worked with the design team to rebuild the saved items page

acceptance_examples.original: Candidates could not upload their portfolios on mobile, so I rebuilt the upload page for small screens, and completion rose from 41% to 68%

user_need.text: Candidates could not upload their portfolios on mobile

action.text: I rebuilt the upload page for small screens

acceptance_examples.notes: Feature appears inside the action sentence; the permitted overlap applies. Metric uses a from-X-to-Y range.

acceptance_examples.original: Hiring managers spent hours screening resumes by hand, and I built (with one backend engineer) the screening filter, a rule-based resume ranking tool

user_need.text: Hiring managers spent hours screening resumes by hand

product_feature.text: the screening filter, a rule-based resume ranking tool

action.text: I built (with one backend engineer) the screening filter, a rule-based resume ranking tool

needs_to_be_filled: Result (missing): The bullet does not say what changed after the filter was built or who it helped.
Metric (missing, optional): “one backend engineer” describes the team, not the impact of the work.
acceptance_examples.first_question_after_yes: Achievement 2 of 3 – Result: What changed after your work? Who did it help?
acceptance_examples.notes: A feature may be a description in an appositive, not only a page name. A team-size number is not a metric.

acceptance_examples.original: Job seekers needed a one-page resume, so I designed the print layout, delivering a one-page PDF export

user_need.text: Job seekers needed a one-page resume

needs_to_be_filled: Result (vague): “delivering a one-page PDF export” describes what you produced, not what changed for the job seeker or who benefited.
Metric (missing, optional): The bullet contains no number that demonstrates the impact of the work.
acceptance_examples.first_question_after_yes: Achievement 1 of 2 – Result: What changed after your work? Who did it help?
acceptance_examples.notes: An output-only result (what was produced, not what changed) is vague.

test_bullets.original: New visitors abandoned the sign-up form halfway, so I simplified the sign-up form to three fields, and sign-ups grew by 25%

user_need.text: New visitors abandoned the sign-up form halfway

action.text: I simplified the sign-up form to three fields

test_bullets.purpose: missing need and vague action (Example 2 pattern)
test_bullets.original: Worked on the search filters and improved them, which increased searches by 9%

action.text: Worked on the search filters and improved them

questions_after_yes: Achievement n – User need or problem: Who had a problem? What was the problem?
Achievement n – Action: What exactly did you do? What was your role?

test_bullets.original: Noticed employers were ignoring long resumes, so I led the rewrite of the resume summary section to make resumes easier to scan

user_need.text: Noticed employers were ignoring long resumes

action.text: I led the rewrite of the resume summary section

result.text: to make resumes easier to scan

questions_after_yes: Achievement n – Result: What changed after your work? Who did it help?
Achievement n – Metric: Do you have a real number? If not, you can skip this.

test_bullets.purpose: research number stays in Action; feature includes the parenthetical; complete bullet
test_bullets.original: Students were dropping out of long courses, so I defined the course progress bar (milestones and badges) through 5 interviews, and course completions grew by 15%

user_need.text: Students were dropping out of long courses

product_feature.text: the course progress bar (milestones and badges)

action.text: I defined the course progress bar (milestones and badges) through 5 interviews

test_bullets.purpose: only a discovery verb; everything except the need is missing
test_bullets.original: Researched why new hires quit within their first year

user_need.text: Researched why new hires quit within their first year

test_bullets.notes: The discovery verb belongs in the need (Problem 2); the need is filled because it names who (new hires) and the problem (quitting in the first year).
questions_after_yes: Achievement n – Product feature: What was the feature or product part you worked on?
Achievement n – Action: What exactly did you do? What was your role?
Achievement n – Result: What changed after your work? Who did it help?
Achievement n – Metric: Do you have a real number? If not, you can skip this.

test_bullets.purpose: trap: a number in the need must not become the metric; the feature must not share words with the need
test_bullets.original: 2,000 job seekers complained the app kept crashing, so I fixed the upload flow, and support tickets about uploads fell by 40%

user_need.text: 2,000 job seekers complained the app kept crashing

test_bullets.notes: “2,000” stays inside the need (it sizes the problem, not the impact). “The app” from the need must not be reused as the feature; the feature comes from the action sentence through the permitted overlap.

test_bullets.purpose: a capability/scope counts as a feature (Problem 1); complete bullet
test_bullets.original: Small shop owners could not sell outside their city, so I scoped and launched the marketplace listings tool (bulk upload and pricing rules), and seller signups grew by 22%

user_need.text: Small shop owners could not sell outside their city

product_feature.text: the marketplace listings tool (bulk upload and pricing rules)

action.text: I scoped and launched the marketplace listings tool (bulk upload and pricing rules)

test_bullets.original: Job seekers could not see where their resumes stood, so I built the application tracker, and weekly active users rose 30%

user_need.text: Job seekers could not see where their resumes stood

test_bullets.notes: A model that writes “rose 30%” entirely in Result and leaves Metric missing fails this test.

test_bullets.purpose: trap: intention phrasing in the result (Problem 4)
test_bullets.original: Employers took too long to pick candidates, so I worked on the review queue so that picking would take minutes instead of hours

user_need.text: Employers took too long to pick candidates

action.text: I worked on the review queue

result.text: picking would take minutes instead of hours

test_bullets.notes: The second “so that” phrase is an intention, so the result is vague; presenting it as a complete result fails this test. A model that is unsure must ask a short question about the result instead of guessing.
questions_after_yes: Achievement n – Action: What exactly did you do? What was your role?
Achievement n – Result: What changed after your work? Who did it help?
Achievement n – Metric: Do you have a real number? If not, you can skip this.

test_bullets.purpose: question discipline: only the metric question, once, at the very end
test_bullets.original: Users could not find their past orders, so I designed the order history page, which made reordering easy

user_need.text: Users could not find their past orders

action.text: I designed the order history page

test_bullets.notes: The only question is the Metric question, asked once, at the very end. Asking about any other section fails this test.
questions_after_yes: Achievement n – Metric: Do you have a real number? If not, you can skip this.

display_frame: Analysis of [user need or problem] and collaboration with the product team on designing [feature name] through [specific action], resulting in [result] and [metric]. — inside brackets only the job seeker's verbatim words; empty = '[label - missing]', ambiguous = '[label: words - vague]'; always 'resulting in [result: ...]', even for vague results.
